taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 3 subtasks, read from the schema reply
5 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
All twelve codes are covered by the three worker reports. They agree with each other, and nothing was left unfinished. I did not open any pages myself, so everything below rests on what the workers reported.

The current HTTP Semantics specification is RFC 9110 (STD 97, June 2022), at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html. All three workers found no "Obsoleted by" notice on it and no newer replacement in search. It obsoletes RFC 7231 and others.

Section 15.1 of that page lists the heuristically cacheable codes as "200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501 in this specification", and says all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable.

- **Cacheable:** 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501 are in that list.
- **Not cacheable:** 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422 are not in the list, and their own sections say nothing about heuristic cacheability.
- **Renamed codes:** 413 is now "Content Too Large" (RFC 7231 called it "Payload Too Large"). 422 is now "Unprocessable Content" (older RFCs called it "Unprocessable Entity").
- **Quote formatting:** the workers joined some quotes across line breaks so they read as single sentences.
